summary: Notto R. Thelle worked in religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He was Associate Director at the NCC Center for the Study of Japanese Religions in 1974 and held a post at the University of Oslo from circa 1986 to 2006.

Specializing in Indology and history/archaeology, Noémie Verdon earned her PhD from the University of Lausanne in 2015 under Johannes Bronkhorst and Charles Genequand. She held an attested post at Kyoto University in 2019.

Noël Péri was a Japanology and Buddhist studies scholar who taught Western music at Tokyo Music School (1896–1906) and founded Mélanges japonais (1904). He later served as resident (1907) and secretary-librarian (1911) at École Française d'Extrême-Orient.
Active in Buddhist and religious studies, Nyanabodhi studied under the traditional teacher Ayya Khema and later succeeded her.

Nyanaponika Thera, a Buddhist studies scholar, studied at the University of Peradeniya and under Nyanatiloka Mahathera and Mahasi Sayadaw. He founded the Buddhist Publication Society, serving as director and editor (1958–1984) and president (~1958–1988).

Nyingcha Duoji specializes in Tibetology. He studied at Boston University and earned a PhD from Harvard University (attested 2014) under doctoral supervisor Leonard van der Kuijp and teacher Mark Elliott.
Nyo Shul Lungtok Tenpé Gyaltsen studied under Patrul Rinpoche, Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo. He also taught Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.

Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Kathok and Nyoshul Monasteries under teachers including Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje, Dilgo Khyentse, Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.
Nyoten Jinbo was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Baisen Azegami. He held a professorship at Komazawa University.

Active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Ogyen Trinley Dorje studied under Khenchen Thrangu Rinpoche, Tenzin Gyatso, Bokar Rinpoche, Drub Pön Dechen Rinpoche, Dragpa Tenpa Yarpel, and Pema Donyo Nyinje.

Olaf Hansen was an Iranian, Central Asian, and linguistics scholar. He held posts at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1937–1944), the University of Jena (~1944–1945), and the Free University of Berlin (~1950–1969).

A scholar of linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology, Olav Hackstein studied at Freiburg, Pennsylvania, and Halle-Wittenberg. He taught at Pennsylvania, Halle-Wittenberg, and EPHE, becoming a full professor at the University of Munich in 2008.
Ole Holten Pind specialized in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He completed his Dr.phil. at the University of Vienna (~2004–2009) under the supervision of Ernst Steinkellner.

Oleg Grabar was an art historian and Central Asianist who studied at Paris, Harvard, and Princeton (PhD ~1955). He taught at the University of Michigan (1954–1969), Harvard University (1969–1990), and the Institute for Advanced Study (1990–1998).

Working in history, archaeology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, Oliver Codrington served as Secretary of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (attested 1878) and Honorary Librarian of the Royal Asiatic Society (attested 1892).

Oliver Hector de Alwis Wijesekera studied at University College, Colombo, and earned his PhD at SOAS under William Stede. An Indology and Buddhist studies scholar, he was Head of Sanskrit at the University of Peradeniya from 1943.
Oliver Philipp Frey is an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Vienna and later held a post there.

Olivier Lacombe was an Indology, philosophy, and religious studies scholar. He studied at the École Normale Supérieure and Faculty of Arts of Paris, later holding posts at the Faculty of Arts of Paris (~1959–1970) and Paris-Sorbonne University (~1970–1974).

Olle Qvarnström works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at Lund, Washington, Harvard, and Copenhagen under Tord Olsson, Karl H. Potter, Collett Cox, and Christian Lindtner, and held a post at Lund University (attested 2000–2005).

Om Prakash earned his PhD at the University of Delhi under Dasharatha Sharma. Specializing in history, archaeology, and Indology, he taught at Kirori Mal College, the University of Delhi, and the Delhi School of Economics.
